headline: High: Copilot can write and modify repo state while Opik has broad egress, creating a plausible data-leak and action-cascade path; prompt-injection risk is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while Opik only exposes a REST API and broad egress; no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented. The pairwise injection path is therefore possible only through manual content transfer or an undocumented integration, so I rate it low rather than none because uncertainty must escalate.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Opik output into Copilot chat or files, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF an undocumented bridge is added between Copilot and Opik, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Do not paste Opik output into Copilot without review.
Disable any custom connector or automation between the two.
Use a provenance note when transferring text between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and can write repo files; Opik has broad network egress and a REST API surface. Even without a documented shared filesystem, the pair can leak code or buffer contents if Opik receives Copilot-produced artifacts or if either side forwards sensitive context to its backend. This exists in default workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated code or buffers are sent into Opik for evaluation, source content may leave the workspace.
IF Opik is configured to transmit traces or prompts containing repo snippets, leakage expands beyond the local machine.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and proprietary files from any evaluation payload.
Use a redaction step before sending artifacts to Opik.
Restrict Opik projects to non-sensitive repositories.
Review outbound payloads for code and credentials before submission.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Opik exposes only a REST API and broad egress with no write capability shown. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope, so direct conflict is limited; uncertainty remains because Opik's full write surfaces are not described, but the known overlap is small.
conditions: IF Opik is wrapped in an external automation that writes the same repo, write conflicts become more likely.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable checkout, git contention can occur.
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access to the repo at a time.
Use separate branches for Copilot edits and Opik outputs.
Add a manual merge step before committing.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same working tree.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits and Workspace plans, and Opik can consume outputs through its REST API, so a workflow where Opik treats Copilot output as authoritative is plausible. Copilot's outputs are not inherently verified by Opik, and Opik's observability/evaluation role can amplify mistaken code or labels into downstream actions or reports. The pathway exists in default integrations, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Opik ingests Copilot-generated text without a verification gate, errors can cascade.
IF Copilot edits are auto-exported into Opik dashboards or evaluations, mistaken outputs can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before Opik consumes Copilot output.
Add schema validation to any Copilot-to-Opik transfer.
Tag Copilot-generated artifacts as untrusted.
Compare outputs against source files before acting on them.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress, while Opik is open-source with broad egress and no stated sensitive-data classes. The pair does not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps around code retention and telemetry rather than a clear breach.
conditions: IF sensitive code is subject to a no-external-processing policy, Copilot use may violate it.
IF Opik is deployed with retention settings that exceed local policy, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Confirm both tools' retention settings.
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document which repositories may be used with Copilot.
Review vendor terms before enabling telemetry.
